name: H5N1 bird flu
value: Cattle-linked US cases; no human spread
summary: US H5N1 cases remain linked to animals after a fatal Washington case on 1 Nov; no sustained human spread found
state: Washington state reported the first US H5N1 death of 2026 on 1 Nov, in Yakima County, and health officials said the risk to the public was low (CNN, 2 Nov). ECDC's early-November summary of human H5N1 cases reports no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission (ECDC). Searches to 16 Nov found no new human cluster, so these remain animal-to-human cases and the level stays Normal.
for_you: UKHSA advises not touching sick or dead birds and reporting them to Defra; the risk to the general public is rated low.

sources.title: CNN — Washington reports first US bird flu death of 2026

why: H5N1 is the flu strain scientists most fear could become a pandemic; it has spread to mammals and dairy cattle.
drivers: Human cases, mammal-to-mammal spread, mutations, surveillance.
